Agreed to send quickstart and free credits, run a small benchmark, and schedule a deeper technical demo.
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-03-25 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~45 minutes | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Head of ML), Ethan (Platform), Sofia (Security)

[00:00:01] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Quick intro?
[00:00:08] Priya: Hi, I'm Priya, Head of ML at Catalyst Solutions, we build an internal assistant and a set of embeddings-based search tools.
[00:00:16] Ethan: Ethan, platform eng, responsible for infra and costs.
[00:00:19] Sofia: Sofia, security and compliance.
[00:00:22] Diego: Diego, SE on the inference side. I'll cover technical questions and benchmarks.

[00:00:30] Maya: Cool. High level — today's goal is to understand your usage patterns, constraints, timeline, and get you up to speed on Redwood's PLG quickstart: free credits, SDKs, time-to-first-token, and the differences between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.

[00:01:05] Priya: We're primarily evaluating hosted first for speed, but we need to know when Dedicated or Private makes sense. Our main questions: latency targets (~100-200ms for single-turn chat), cost per 1M tokens, and how long to get a PoC running — like time to first token.

[00:01:40] Diego: For the PLG quickstart, you can sign up, get a one-time free credits code, and call the Redwood API in minutes. We have SDKs (Python/JS) and example notebooks — typical time-to-first-token for devs is under 10 minutes if you follow the quickstart.

[00:02:05] Ethan: Nice. For our infra, we need to know about rate limits and quotas, and how the billing looks — per-token or other.

[00:02:18] Maya: Hosted is usage-based per-token (generation + embeddings). Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at commit. Private is for VPC/on-prem or air-gapped needs. We can share a pricing sheet but I'll send specifics after.

[00:03:00] Sofia: Security questions: SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration, and data residency — do you have regional hosting? Also retention policies?

[00:03:15] Diego: We are SOC2 and have ISO in progress. Hosted supports region selection for some regions; Dedicated gives stronger isolation and Private gives customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integrations. We also provide audit logs per-route and per-token tracing in the Console.

[00:03:50] Speaker 2: sorry can you run that again about KMS, we had a typo —
[00:03:55] Diego: Yes — KMS integration for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer encryption at rest and in transit and customer-managed keys are available on private plans.

[00:04:20] Priya: About models: do you host open models or proprietary ones? Latency will vary by model.

[00:04:30] Maya: We have a model catalog of curated open models and Redwood-verified profiles. For low-latency single-turn we recommend smaller distilled variants or quantized weights on Dedicated. Hosted has multiple model options with performance tiers.

[00:05:10] Ethan: If we start Hosted and then commit to Dedicated, what's the migration path? We don't want to rework code.

[00:05:20] Diego: The API is the same across modes. You can pin model versions and rollout policies; switching from Hosted to Dedicated is largely config and routing, not code changes.

[00:06:00] Priya: Can we run a quick benchmark using our prompts? We're interested in P95 latency and cost per 1k tokens.

[00:06:10] Diego: Absolutely. Typical plan: you share a representative prompt set, we run a small benchmark on Hosted (or a Dedicated dev pool if you have committed capacity) and provide latency/cost breakdown per model. It usually takes a few days.

[00:06:40] Maya: We'll give you one-time free credits to run initial tests and the quickstart guide with code snippets.

[00:07:05] Sofia: We also need to know about logging of prompt/response content and retention. For compliance we cannot retain user PII beyond X days.

[00:07:15] Diego: You can configure retention policies and disable logging for certain routes; Private gives the most control. Hosted can be configured per-customer with retention settings and redaction options.

[00:08:00] Ethan: What about tokenization differences — do you have consistent token counts across models? We want predictable costing when switching models.

[00:08:12] Diego: Tokenization can vary by model family. Our Console provides token-level cost breakdowns so you can compare expected unit economics across candidate models. We also recommend a profiling step in the benchmark.

[00:09:05] Priya: In terms of integration, does Redwood support streaming and function/tool calling? We use streaming for progressive UI.

[00:09:18] Maya: Yes, hosted API supports streaming and function/tool calling. SDKs have examples.

[00:09:45] Priya: Any gotchas for running embeddings at scale? We're planning an embeddings index for search with frequent updates.

[00:09:55] Diego: Embeddings are per-unit billed, and we have cache and batching recommendations in Redwood Optimize to reduce cost. For frequent updates, consider incremental re-embedding and smart caching.

[00:10:30] Ethan: How about observability — do you provide per-route dashboards and traces? We need to tie tokens and latency back to our app routes for alerting.

[00:10:38] Maya: Redwood Console has per-route/model dashboards, token-level costs, tracing hooks, and error analysis. We can provide screenshots and a trial account.

[00:11:05] Sofia: For SSO, we use Okta. SAML support?

[00:11:12] Diego: Yes, SAML/Okta is supported for Console access. For API keys you can integrate with centralized secrets manager and RBAC policies.

[00:12:00] Priya: About fallbacks — if the primary model or region is saturated, do you have graceful degradation?

[00:12:08] Diego: Smart routing and automatic fallback policies exist; you can route by latency/cost/region and fallback to compatible model variants. This is useful during spikes.

[00:12:40] Speaker 3: there's a little bit of crosstalk —
[00:12:44] Maya: Sorry, just to recap what we recommend for your PoC: start with Hosted using free credits, run a small benchmark on your prompt set, evaluate latency and cost, then decide on Dedicated if you need predictable throughput or Private for strict compliance.

[00:13:20] Priya: Timeline: we'd like a PoC in two weeks, but security review will take longer.

[00:13:30] Sofia: We'll need SOC2 documentation and answers about key management and retention for legal.

[00:13:40] Maya: I'll send SOC2 summary, the security whitepaper, and the quickstart guide with the free credits code. Diego will draft a benchmark plan.

[00:14:05] Ethan: For the benchmark, can you include steps to measure P50/P95, cost per 1k tokens, and a sample script?

[00:14:15] Diego: Yes, plan will include sample scripts (Python/Node), instructions for streaming vs batch, and how to interpret results in the Console.

[00:14:40] Priya: Any red flags we should know about — like data residency limits on Hosted?

[00:14:48] Diego: Hosted region availability varies; if your data residency requires specific region or air-gapped environments, Private is the recommended path.

[00:15:20] Maya: Also note, quantization and kernel selection affect latency; for P95 <200ms we may recommend a smaller quantized variant on Dedicated.

[00:15:50] Ethan: What's the typical uplift in throughput for Dedicated vs Hosted?

[00:15:58] Diego: Dedicated pools are provisioned on GPU and you get predictable throughput; unit cost is usually lower at commit but you trade off flexibility.

[00:16:20] Priya: Are there any known issues with long-context sessions and KV cache? We use long conversation histories.

[00:16:30] Diego: Our runtime supports KV cache management and prefix caching. For very long contexts we recommend chunking strategies and indexing.

[00:17:05] Speaker 1: mm-hmm
[00:17:10] Priya: Great. I think action items are clear. A few smaller Qs: is there a sandbox org so our infra can poke at the API and measure e2e latency from our VPC?

[00:17:22] Maya: Yes, we can create a trial org with credits; for e2e latency from your VPC you'll need to run client-side tests or set up a small agent in your network. For Private we can deploy closer to you.

[00:17:50] Ethan: For cost forecasting, will we be able to export token-level metrics?

[00:17:58] Diego: Yes, Console exports and APIs for usage data exist.

[00:18:20] Sofia: One more about encryption — any customer-managed KMS for Hosted?

[00:18:26] Maya: Customer-managed keys are primarily available on Private plans, but we can discuss options for Hosted enterprise customers.

[00:19:00] Priya: Ok. Next steps?

[00:19:05] Maya: I'll follow up with: quickstart guide + free credits, SOC2 doc, pricing sheet. Diego will share benchmark plan. We'll set up a technical demo with infra next week — propose Wed 2026-03-31.

[00:19:30] Priya: Wed works for us tentatively.

[00:19:40] Maya: Anything else?

[00:19:43] Ethan: Not from me.

[00:19:45] Sofia: No.

[00:19:47] Priya: Thanks, helpful.

[00:20:00] Maya: Great — recap: Catalyst will sign up, use free credits to run a quick test; Priya share prompt set, Diego will run bench and we reconvene after results. I'll send the resources and free credits code.

[00:20:25] Diego: Thanks everyone.

Meeting end (participants lingered for a minute to chat)

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., "Dedicate" instead of Dedicated, "KV cash"), natural pauses and crosstalk. The transcript contains security and compliance topics and explicit next steps to share quickstart + credits and run benchmark.
